Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Phaser 4 WebGL: migrate core `GeometryMask` sites to Mask filters + scaffold `Phaser.AUTO`

Raised from `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` (Main Street repo, `../tce-main-street`) on producer
instruction (2026-10-29, "separate core item in `../Tableau-Card-Engine`").

## Problem statement

Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7` made `GameObject.setMask` a **no-op under WebGL**.
`node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/components/Mask.js:27` states
`GeometryMask` is Canvas-only; the WebGL path logs

```
Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method is not supported in WebGL. Create a Mask filter instead.
```

and returns immediately, so the object renders **unclipped**.

The Main Street game repo has completed its side of the migration
(`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`, commit `73cfba6c` on its `dev`) and has switched its
launcher from `Phaser.CANVAS` to `Phaser.AUTO`. That change makes this defect
live in shipped builds: the core-owned overlays below lose their scroll
clipping in any WebGL boot.

Outstanding core-owned call sites (verified 2026-10-29 against core `f0b5b9e9`):

- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — `setMask` at the scroll-region setup
  (observed at `SettingsPanel.ts:574` during a real WebGL boot)
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — `setupScrollMask` (observed at `HelpPanel.ts:386`)
- `src/ui/Overlay.ts` — `setMask` / `createGeometryMask` in the overlay dialog
  scroll region
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts` — `setMask`
  (reached via `GymSceneBase.initHelp`)

Additionally the scaffold generator still forces Canvas, so every downstream
game repo it generates reverts the migration:

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderMainTs()` emits `type: Phaser.CANVAS`
- the core repo's own `main.ts` likewise

## Users

- **Game players** — Help / Settings / Overlay dialogs and the Gym card index
  must stay visually correct (content clipped to its scroll region) in WebGL
  builds, not just in Canvas ones.
- **Downstream game-repo maintainers** — need the scaffold to emit
  `Phaser.AUTO` so a fresh/re-scaffolded repo does not silently regress to
  Canvas and lose access to Phaser 4's Filter/GPU-shader pipeline.
- **Maintainers** — one shared core helper instead of per-repo copies.

## Reference implementation (already proven, do not re-invent)

`../tce-main-street/src/ContainerClip.ts` is the working pattern and is the
model to port into core as a shared, exported helper:

- `createContainerClip(scene, target, rect?)` branches once on
  `scene.renderer.type`:
  - **Canvas**: unchanged `GeometryMask` (transparent fill, Graphics on the
    display list) — Canvas output stays byte-stable.
  - **WebGL**: `target.enableFilters()` then
    `target.filters.internal.addMask(graphics, false, scene.cameras.main)`,
    with an **opaque** fill and the Graphics kept **off the display list**
    (a Mask filter samples the mask texture's alpha and renders the mask
    GameObject itself).
- **`clear()` is a real "no clip"** (Canvas `clearMask`, WebGL
  `filter.active = false`). A zero-area mask is *not* a no-op — it hides the
  whole object.
- A `Container` has no intrinsic width/height, so Phaser focuses the filter on
  the camera context and the mask applies in **screen space**, matching Canvas
  `GeometryMask` semantics (fixed to the scene, not following the object).
- Tear down the clip on scene shutdown: under WebGL the mask Graphics is off
  the display list and is not disposed by the scene.
- Verified by evidence: a Mask filter **does** clip a `Container` in rc.7;
  proven with `renderer.snapshotPixel()` probes inside/outside the rect, and
  unchanged when the clipped container is translated. No per-camera-viewport
  fallback is needed.

Do not edit the Main Street repo from this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Core helper.** A renderer-aware container-clip helper exists in core
   (suggested `src/ui/ContainerClip.ts`), exported through the public `@ui`
   surface so downstream game repos can reuse it, with the `ContainerClip`
   API (`setRect`, `clear`, `destroy`) and the Canvas/WebGL branching described
   above. Its doc comment records the Phaser 4 Canvas-only `setMask`
   restriction.
2. **Sites migrated.** `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`, `src/ui/Overlay.ts`,
   `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` and `example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts`
   no longer construct a `GeometryMask` directly for clipping; all four use the
   shared helper.
3. **Scaffold emits `Phaser.AUTO`.** `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`
   `renderMainTs()` emits `type: Phaser.AUTO`, the core repo's own `main.ts`
   matches, and any scaffold test/fixture asserting `Phaser.CANVAS` is updated.
4. **WebGL browser test.** At least one browser test forces `Phaser.WEBGL` and
   asserts (a) clipping actually happens (pixel probe via
   `renderer.snapshotPixel()`) and (b) **no** `setMask … not supported in
   WebGL` warning is emitted from core code. Canvas parity is asserted in the
   same file.
5. **No Canvas regression.** Full core test suite green; Canvas rendering
   output unchanged (the Canvas branch keeps `GeometryMask`).
6. **Docs.** The renderer/mask restriction is documented (core README and/or
   `docs/`) so the next reader does not repeat the diagnosis, and the scaffold
   documentation states the emitted renderer.
7. **Downstream switch-over hand-off.** On completion, a work item is created
   (or the existing placeholder updated) in the Main Street repo
   (`../tce-main-street`) to: bump the pinned core commit in
   `configs/engine-pin.json`, run `npm run scaffold` to regenerate
   `main.ts`, re-run `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts`
   with the core-owned warnings no longer excluded, and confirm the launcher
   boots WebGL with no unclipped core overlay.
   **The follow-up already exists**: `MS-0MVTMJ2GA008GRZ7` ("Re-scaffold Main
   Street launcher to Phaser.AUTO and verify a clean WebGL boot once core masks
   land") in the Main Street store, currently `blocked`. Reuse/update that item
   rather than creating a second one, and leave a comment on it naming the core
   commit that satisfies this item.

## Constraints

- Do **not** edit the Main Street repo (`../tce-main-street`) from this item;
  the cross-repo hand-off is a work-item, not a code edit (AC7).
- Canvas behaviour must not change: branch on the renderer, do not replace the
  `GeometryMask` path.
- No new dependencies.
- `TestGamePool` and downstream browser tests intentionally stay on
  `Phaser.CANVAS` for CI speed (~10x faster under SwiftShader) — do not force
  them to WebGL.

## Existing state / verified facts

- Phaser pin: `4.0.0-rc.7`. `GameObject` mixes in `Components.Filters`
  (`enableFilters()`, `filters`), so any GameObject — `Container` included —
  can host a Mask filter.
- `GeometryMask` uses the Graphics **path** and ignores fill alpha; a Mask
  filter uses the rendered mask texture's **alpha**.
- `filterList.getActive()` filters on `filter.active`, so `active = false` is a
  cheap way to disable a clip without destroying it.

## Related work

- `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` (Main Street) — renderer migration + renderer-aware
  clips for the in-repo surfaces; delivered commit `73cfba6c`. Source of this
  item.
- `MS-0MVT4M9KM005Z0YM` (Main Street) — the original diagnosis; closed as a
  duplicate of `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`, with its core-owned part routed here.
- `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW` (Main Street) — the earlier core-deferral record for
  `HelpPanel` / `Overlay` / `SettingsPanel`; superseded by this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: filter cost.** Each clipped container gains a filter render step
  (context-sized for unbounded containers). Mitigation: measure in the browser
  test scene; keep the clip count small (4 sites).
- **Risk: Mask filter on a nested/transformed container.** The Main Street
  evidence covers transformed containers; re-verify per core site with a pixel
  probe rather than assuming.
- **Assumption:** headless Chromium (Playwright) provides WebGL2 in CI, so the
  WebGL browser test is viable.
data.title: Phaser 4 WebGL: migrate core GeometryMask sites to Mask filters + scaffold Phaser.AUTO

# Goal

As a core maintainer, I want one reusable browser-test harness that boots a scene
under a **forced** renderer, captures console warnings, and probes framebuffer
pixels — so every renderer-parity assertion in this migration is a few lines and
cannot silently pass on the wrong renderer.

Parent: `CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I` (AC4 needs a WebGL pixel probe + "no `setMask` warning"
assertion; no core test does either today — `renderer.snapshotPixel()` is used
only in the Main Street repo).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/helpers/bootRendererScene.ts` exports `bootRendererScene(renderType)`
  which creates the game with the requested `Phaser.CANVAS` / `Phaser.WEBGL`
  type, awaits scene active, asserts `scene.renderer.type === renderType`, and
  registers teardown (game destroy + canvas-pool drain via `phaserCanvasPool`).
- It exports a console-warning capture (`captureConsoleWarnings(scene?)`) that
  records every `console.warn` emitted between start and stop, with the message
  text available for assertion.
- It exports `probePixel(scene, x, y)` built on `renderer.snapshotPixel()`,
  returning a comparable colour value, and documented as requiring a rendered
  frame (helper awaits a render tick first).
- Environments without WebGL fail **loudly**: the harness reports a recorded
  skip reason (never a green pass), and the self-test asserts the renderer type
  it actually got.
- `tests/helpers/bootRendererScene.browser.test.ts` proves the harness itself:
  boots under CANVAS and WEBGL, warning capture sees a synthetic `console.warn`,
  `probePixel` returns the expected background colour.

- `tests/helpers/bootRendererScene.ts`
- `tests/helpers/bootRendererScene.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/helpers/phaserCanvasPool.ts`
- `tests/helpers/waitForScene.ts`

# Goal

As a game developer depending on the engine, I want a core-owned, exported
renderer-aware container clip so a WebGL boot clips panel content exactly like a
Canvas boot does — and downstream repos stop carrying their own copies.

Port the proven pattern from `../tce-main-street/src/ContainerClip.ts`
(do **not** re-invent it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Core helper.** A renderer-aware container-clip helper exists in core, exported
  through the public `@ui` surface with the `ContainerClip` API (`setRect`,
  `clear`, `destroy`) and the Canvas/WebGL branching described below.
- **WebGL browser test.** At least one browser test forces `Phaser.WEBGL` and
  asserts clipping actually happens (pixel probe via `renderer.snapshotPixel()`)
  and that no `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warning is emitted from core
  code; Canvas parity is asserted in the same file.
- `src/ui/ContainerClip.ts` exports `createContainerClip(scene, target, rect?)`
  and the `ContainerClip` interface (`renderer`, `graphics`, `geometryMask`,
  `maskFilter`, `rect`, `active`, `setRect`, `clear`, `destroy`), plus
  `isWebGLRenderer(scene)`; both are exported from `src/ui/index.ts` so
  downstream repos import them from `@ui`.
- Canvas branch keeps today's behaviour: transparent-fill `GeometryMask`,
  Graphics on the display list, `clearMask()` on `clear()` — Canvas rendering
  output is unchanged.
- WebGL branch: `target.enableFilters()` then
  `target.filters.internal.addMask(graphics, false, scene.cameras.main)`; the
  mask Graphics is created with `scene.make.graphics(..., false)` (**off** the
  display list) and drawn **opaque**; a missing filter list (no WebGL context)
  degrades to `maskFilter === null` without throwing.
- `clear()` is a real "no clip" on both renderers, and `destroy()` is
  idempotent and removes the filter / mask resources.
- The module doc comment records the Phaser 4 (`4.0.0-rc.7`) restriction —
  `GameObject.setMask` logs "not supported in WebGL" and no-ops — and why the
  mask must be opaque and off the display list.
- Unit tests (`tests/ui/ContainerClip.test.ts`) cover renderer branch selection,
  `clear()`/`destroy()` idempotence and post-destroy no-ops, using stubs.
- Browser test (`tests/ui/ContainerClip.browser.test.ts`), written **before**
  the helper (TDD): under `Phaser.WEBGL` a clipped container's content is
  visible inside the rect and absent outside it (`renderer.snapshotPixel()`
  probe), the result is unchanged when the container is translated (screen-space
  mask), **and no** `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warning is captured;
  the same file asserts Canvas parity (clip applied via `GeometryMask`).

## Key Files

- `src/ui/ContainerClip.ts`
- `src/ui/index.ts`
- `tests/ui/ContainerClip.test.ts`
- `tests/ui/ContainerClip.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/helpers/bootRendererScene.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked-by `CG-0MVTQ3UFI009LH8Q` (WebGL clip test harness).

## Deliverables

- Helper + exports + unit tests + WebGL/Canvas browser parity test green;
  `npm run build` green.

# Goal

As a player on a WebGL boot, I want the Help panel, overlay dialog and Settings
panel scroll areas clipped to their visible region so overflowing content no
longer draws over panel chrome and the scene behind it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Sites migrated.** `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`, `src/ui/Overlay.ts`,
  `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` and `example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts`
  no longer construct a `GeometryMask` directly for clipping; the three core UI
  sites in this item use the shared helper (the Gym scene is `CG-0MVTQ3W58004XN92`).
- **No Canvas regression.** Full core test suite green; Canvas rendering output
  unchanged (the Canvas branch keeps `GeometryMask`).
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` (`setupScrollMask`), `src/ui/Overlay.ts`
  (`refresh()`) and `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` (the `_maxContentY > canvasHeight`
  branch) no longer construct `Phaser.Display.Masks.GeometryMask`; all three use
  `createContainerClip()` from `@ui/ContainerClip`.
- Under WebGL the mask Graphics is **off** the display list for all three
  (including `HelpPanel`, which currently adds it via `scene.add.graphics()` and
  exposes it in its children list).
- Re-clipping follows existing geometry: `setRect()` is applied on scroll mask
  updates, on panel slide-in/reposition and on resize; `clear()` is used when
  there is nothing to clip (`maxScroll <= 0` / content fits) — a zero-area rect
  is never used to mean "no clip".
- Teardown: `HelpPanel.destroy()` and `SettingsPanel.destroy()` call
  `clip.destroy()`; `Overlay`'s dialog `close()`/`dismissOverlay()` destroys the
  clip with the other overlay objects. `SettingsPanel` gains a tracked clip
  field (it currently keeps no reference to its mask Graphics).
- Full unit + build green; existing Canvas-path panel tests
  (`HelpSettingsButtons.test.ts`, `Overlay.test.ts`, `SettingsPanel.test.ts`,
  `SettingsPanel*.browser.test.ts`) still pass — Canvas output unchanged.
- `tests/ui/CorePanelWebglClip.browser.test.ts` boots each of the three panels
  under `Phaser.WEBGL` and asserts (a) content outside the scroll rect is not
  rendered (pixel probe, not a mock), (b) no core-originated
  `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warning, (c) close → reopen and
  `destroy()` leave no orphaned mask Graphics or active filter; the same file
  asserts Canvas parity for at least one panel.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`
- `src/ui/Overlay.ts`
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`
- `tests/ui/CorePanelWebglClip.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/ui/HelpSettingsButtons.test.ts`
- `tests/ui/Overlay.test.ts`
- `tests/ui/SettingsPanel.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked-by `CG-0MVTQ3UZL004YO8O` (core `ContainerClip` helper).

delete its local `src/ContainerClip.ts` and import the core helper.

# Game-repo scaffold must wire git hooks and emit a full-suite pre-push variant

discovered-from: MS-0MVTI7F5R009OQ14 (tce-main-street)

> **Scope (producer decision, 2026-11-03):** narrowed to the **Tableau-Card-Engine** repo only. The framework hook content and `install_pi.sh` selection are owned by **`SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`** (SorraAgents); this item wires the *scaffold* to activate hooks, seeds thresholds, and verifies the unified gate in a real game repo. **Blocked-by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`.**

## Problem statement

Game repos generated by the engine scaffold (`scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) receive a committed `.githooks/` directory but **no activation**: the scaffold never sets `core.hooksPath`, so git ignores the committed hooks in every fresh clone until someone runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` by hand. The scaffold also generates no `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`, so the context-budget gate is fail-open, and it ships the gate-less **v2** hook rather than the full-suite gate. The full-suite hook *content* (local-then-global runner resolution) is delivered by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`; this item makes the scaffold **produce a push-gated repo that consumes that unified hook** with no manual per-clone activation.

## Users / user stories

- As a **game producer/agent**, I want a freshly scaffolded game repo to have active git hooks, so branch policy, worklog sync and the context-budget gate work without a manual per-clone step.
- As the **producer**, I want scaffolded repos to ship the full-suite pre-push gate, so "pushed to `dev`" means "green at this git state" and the audit skill can reuse a real cache entry.
- As a **framework maintainer**, I want the scaffold and `install_pi.sh` to agree on one hook variant, so game-repo hooks do not drift from the framework's.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Scaffold wires hooks and thresholds.** `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks` in generated repos, installs the full-suite pre-push hook (the unified v3 content from `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`), and generates/commits `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` from the new repo's measured surface. *Metric: scaffold a throwaway repo in a temp dir; assert `git config --get core.hooksPath` is `.githooks`, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves inside `.githooks`, the generated `.githooks/pre-push` carries the full-suite gate (not the gate-less v2), and the thresholds file exists and passes `measure_context.py`.*
- **AC2 — Worktree-safe under `--strict-git-env`.** A push from a linked worktree of a scaffolded repo runs the gate and is gated, with no `--strict-git-env` refusal. *Metric: end-to-end test pushes from a linked worktree with a stub runner and asserts the suite is invoked and the push is gated (git-exported worktree-managed `GIT_DIR` exempt; see `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9).*
- **AC3 — Rollout verified in a real game repo and documented.** Re-run the scaffold/installer against `../tce-main-street`, confirm `core.hooksPath` and the full-suite gate on a real `dev` push (a gate-produced full-suite cache entry exists), and update the scaffold/README notes plus TCE-owned docs. *Metric: rollout evidence recorded on this item; docs updated; full engine suite passes.*
- **AC4 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and the TCE-owned `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (scaffold activation, threshold generation, the one-activation-step-on-fresh-clone caveat). Stale claims that game repos cannot have the gate are removed.
- **AC5 — Tests green.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (run via the test skill).

## Constraints

- **Tableau-Card-Engine repo only.** The framework hook content and `install_pi.sh` selection live in SorraAgents under `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`; do **not** edit SorraAgents from this item. Consume that item's unified v3 hook.
- POSIX `sh` hook; no new runtime dependencies; the hook must keep working on a bare git checkout.
- Do not weaken the existing v2 gates (branch policy, context budget, worklog sync) or their bypass variables.
- Keep the gate fail-*closed* for a missing runner on `dev`/`main`; fail-open remains acceptable only for optional tooling (context-budget measurement).
- Preserve scaffold idempotence. Setting `core.hooksPath` is **local config**, so the scaffold must document that a fresh clone still needs one activation step (`install_pi.sh` or `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`).
- Respect the project test-execution policy: no ad-hoc suite invocation; use the test skill.

## Existing state

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — no `githooks` / `hooksPath` / thresholds handling (grep returns nothing); it writes a fixed set of rendered root files (`package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `main.ts`, `env.d.ts`, `index.html`) plus a preset.
- TCE `.githooks/pre-push` — **v2** (branch policy + context budget + worklog sync), no full-suite gate.
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` — refreshes `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` for the current repo (resolves `measure_context.py` local-then-global).
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — existing scaffold suite (temp fixtures, no network); no hook-wiring assertions.
- `../tce-main-street` (evidence repo) — `.githooks/` committed (v2), `core.hooksPath` unset, no thresholds file, no repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; `.git/hooks/pre-push` is an unversioned manual copy.
- `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` (SorraAgents, `intake_complete`) — owns the unified v3 hook (local→global runner), one-variant `install_pi.sh`, installed-hook upgrade, and the framework `docs/dev/context-budget.md` table.

## Desired change

1. In `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, set `core.hooksPath=.githooks` in generated repos and install the full-suite pre-push hook (the unified v3 content from `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`) instead of the gate-less v2.
2. Generate and commit `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` for generated repos from their measured surface (reuse `measure_context.py --generate-thresholds` via `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh`).
3. Extend `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` with temp-repo assertions (hooks path, hooks-dir resolution, hook content/gate, thresholds validity) and a linked-worktree push test with a stub runner.
4. Roll out to `../tce-main-street`: set `core.hooksPath`, install the full-suite hook, generate thresholds, and verify a `dev` push is gated and produces a full-suite cache entry.
5. Update scaffold docs / `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `README.md` / TCE `docs/dev/context-budget.md`; remove stale claims that game repos cannot have the gate.
6. Document that a fresh clone still needs one activation step (`install_pi.sh` or `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — set `core.hooksPath`, install the unified hook, seed thresholds.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — TCE hook template to align with the unified v3 full-suite variant (coordinate content with `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`; single source of truth, no divergent copy).
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` — threshold-generation entry point.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — hook wiring + thresholds + linked-worktree tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (TCE-owned notes), `README.md` — scaffold/hook docs.
- **Not this item (SorraAgents, owned by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`):** `scripts/install_pi.sh`, `.githooks/pre-push.v2`, framework `docs/dev/context-budget.md`.

## Related work

- **`SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` — blocking.** "Framework pre-push hook v3 should resolve the global test runner" (SorraAgents, `intake_complete`): delivers the unified v3 hook (local→global runner), one-variant `install_pi.sh`, installed-hook upgrade, and the framework docs table. This item consumes that design.
- **`MS-0MVTI7F5R009OQ14`** — `tce-main-street` git hooks inactivity (open): game-side repair of that checkout; the producer deferred the full-suite gate and scaffold wiring to this engine item (answers Q1=c, Q3=a).
- **`SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM`** — original reason non-SorraAgents projects get the v2 hook (they lack `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`); superseded by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` resolving the global runner.
- **`SA-0MSN2ULOF007JJ35`** — AI_Hell v2 rollout: precedent for wiring a real project and verifying the gate end-to-end.
- **`SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61` / `SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`** — scope-aware test gate and the "full suite first runs at the dev-push gate" deferral this item makes real for game repos.
- **`SA-0MT1WUEIT006U1HC`** — automated hook wiring via `install_pi.sh`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — hook blocks every game push.** A runner-resolution bug would stop all `dev` pushes. Mitigate with stub-runner tests, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`, and an explicit fail-closed message naming the remedy. (Unified hook design owned by the SA item.)
- **Risk — hook drift between TCE's template and SorraAgents' hook.** Mitigate by consuming the SA item's content as the single source of truth and documenting the coordination; do not fork the hook.
- **Risk — suite duration at push time.** A game full suite is minutes; acceptable at one `dev` push per work item; the runner cache makes repeat pushes cheap.
- **Risk — host-wide test-slot contention** when a hook holds the runner's lock. Rely on the runner's bounded lock timeout.
- **Assumption — global runner availability.** Game-machine installs include the test skill (`~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`); the fail-closed message names `install_pi.sh` when it is missing.
- **Assumption — scaffold regeneration is safe.** Setting `core.hooksPath` is local config; a fresh clone still needs one activation step (documented).
- **Scope-creep risk:** porting every game repo now, redesigning the context-budget measurement, or editing SorraAgents is out of scope; one rollout repo proves the path.

## Appendix: Research & clarifying questions

Research performed during intake (2026-11-03):

- **Repository split confirmed.** The files named in this brief are not all in the Tableau-Card-Engine repo:
  - `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` and `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` live in **Tableau-Card-Engine** (the earlier `core/scripts/...` path was the view from a game repo where `core/` is the TCE submodule). Grep confirms the scaffold has **no** `githooks` / `hooksPath` / `thresholds` handling today, and writes a fixed set of rendered root files.
  - `scripts/install_pi.sh`, `.githooks/pre-push` (v3), `.githooks/pre-push.v2`, `tests/test_pre_push_context_budget_gate.py` and the framework `docs/dev/context-budget.md` live in the **SorraAgents** framework repo (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`), **not** TCE.
- **Overlapping open work item found.** `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` — "Framework pre-push hook v3 should resolve the global test runner" (SorraAgents, `open`, `intake_complete`, type `chore`) already covers the original brief's AC2 (local→global runner resolution), AC3 (one hook variant from `install_pi.sh`, drop the v2 fallback) and the framework docs variant-table update. Its approach is a **single unified v3 hook**, so a separate `.githooks/pre-push.game` / "v4 unified hook" is unnecessary.
- **Duplicate check performed** (`wl search` on "git hooks pre-push", "install_pi hook", "scaffold hooksPath", "context budget thresholds"): no *completed* duplicate exists; the only overlap is the open SA item above. Scope reconciled per Q1 below.
- **Evidence repo state re-verified** in `../tce-main-street` (2026-11-03): `.githooks/` committed (v2 hook), `core.hooksPath` unset, `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` absent, no repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, and `.git/hooks/pre-push` is an unversioned manual copy.

- **Q1 — Scope reconciliation with `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`.** — Answer (producer, 2026-11-03): **(a)** narrow this CG item to the game-repo scaffold wiring (AC1) + rollout verification (AC3) + worktree test (AC2), and mark it **blocked-by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Repo ownership / cross-project edits.** — Answer (producer, 2026-11-03): **(a)** this CG item edits the **Tableau-Card-Engine repo only** (scaffold + its tests + TCE docs); the framework hook and `install_pi.sh` edits are owned by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Hook variant shape.** — Answer (producer, 2026-11-03): **(a)** one **unified v3 hook** that resolves the runner local-then-global (no separate game variant). Source: interactive reply.
